Composed expressions evaluate branches lazily; host-language arguments to direct functions are evaluated before the function is called. All declared named inputs are required even in untaken branches.

semantics.documented_behavior: Returns value_if_true when logical_test is TRUE and value_if_false when it is FALSE; Microsoft documents the third argument as optional.
semantics.default: An omitted optional value_if_false returns FALSE in the Workbook Forge profile.
semantics.evaluation_profile: Workbook Forge evaluates only the selected result branch. Microsoft documents branch selection but does not specify the evaluator error-order contract.
semantics.explicit_omission_profile: An explicitly empty selected branch returns #VALUE! in Workbook Forge. Microsoft examples and problem notes differ on empty branch slots; this profile has not been checked directly in Excel.
semantics.array_result_profile: A selected generated array preserves its shape through evaluate_result. This formula result is not projected into worksheet spill cells.

functions.reference_scope: Inherited formula documentation; native input/error/resource restrictions in this descriptor take precedence.

semantics.documented_behavior: Returns value_if_error when value evaluates to a supported error; otherwise returns the formula result.
semantics.documented_array_behavior: Microsoft documents element-wise array results for array formulas. Workbook Forge currently passes a generated array through as one shaped result and does not apply value_if_error element-wise to error cells inside arrays or ranges.
semantics.array_result_profile: A selected generated array or array fallback preserves shape through evaluate_result. Worksheet spill placement is unsupported.

Fractional precision is truncated and precision is bounded by the existing Forge evaluator profile.

semantics.direction: nearest; midpoint ties away from zero

precision.negative: round to positions left of the decimal point

semantics.fractional_num_digits: truncated toward zero; Microsoft references do not specify nonintegral precision behavior, so this implementation rule still needs an Excel desktop spot-check
semantics.input_conversion: Scalar inputs use the evaluator numeric coercion: blank to 0, logical to 1 or 0, and numeric text through a locale-independent parser; Excel parity for these coercions is not yet spot-checked.
engine_limits: scalar finite numeric values only; ranges and non-finite inputs are outside this evaluator profile
num_digits is bounded to -308 through 308; values outside this range return #NUM!

omitted_argument: Distinct from blank; supported only as an immediate function-call argument.
input_contract: Case-sensitive ASCII names; every declared input is required and unknown inputs are refused.
evaluation_payload: The 1 MiB limit also applies to compact UTF-8 JSON containing both the expression envelope and encoded inputs. Repeated bound values count at every expression use.
